transcript:
Meeting header:
Date/Time: 2025-03-03 14:00 UTC
Duration: 52 minutes
Attendees: Maya Chen, Samir Patel, Derrick Lee (Redwood) — Lena Voron, Tomás Ruiz, Priya Singh, Eva Martins (SilverGrove)

Summary: quick renewal/check-in to lock extension terms, validate EU on‑prem pilot timeline and technical blockers. Discussed capacity uplift (reserved), VPC/KMS, latency SLOs and benchmarking plan.

[00:00] Maya Chen: hey everyone, thanks for joining, can you hear me ok?
[00:03] Lena Voron: yep, loud and clear. thanks for fitting this in, we wanted to run through the extension and the onprem onramp details.
[00:10] Samir Patel: great — ill start with a short tech readout, then Maya will go over commercial quick, and we'll map next steps. hope that's fine.
[00:18] Tomás Ruiz: sounds good. quick FYI we had an incident last week with our GPU cluster so timing is a little sensitive — we want to have EU onprem ready before Q3 traffic ramp.
[00:29] Priya Singh: yeah and from ML side, the latency tail matters — we saw 95th spike when sequence lengths increased. We want to keep < 220ms p95 for our customer flows.

[00:45] Samir Patel: ok, noted. for the onprem option — Redwood's onprem package uses a private control plane plus an agent set; we support KMS integrations (HSM or cloud KMS), and a VPC peering option. There's a couple of templates we recommend for GCP/Azure, and an airgap flow if you need it.
[01:05] Tomás Ruiz: when you say agent set can you clarify — is that containerized? daemon? we'd prefer a managed appliance but are open.
[01:12] Samir Patel: it's containerized — docker/k8s. most customers run it on k8s; we also provide a small VM-based installer for edge sites. it's not a black box appliance right now. apologies if the docs called it an 'appliance' before.
[01:25] Lena Voron: ok, we can do k8s. question: will logs ever leave our VPC? we need strict data residency.
[01:32] Derrick Lee: good question — by default telemetry is optional; we can turn off outbound telemetry and keep audit logs in your KMS-protected storage. for SOC 2 type requests we provide audit export bundles.
[01:43] Eva Martins: and encryption at rest — HSM support? our security team requires HSM-backed keys.
[01:48] Samir Patel: yes, HSM and customer-managed KMS both supported. small caveat: some older quantized runtime snapshots required a key-wrap flow we had to patch — that was fixed in the last release but i'll confirm the release number in the follow up doc.

[02:10] Priya Singh: on performance — when we tested last quarter on hosted, the cost per 1k tokens was fine, but with our higher throughput forecasts cost gets hairy. we're definitely looking at Dedicated/reserved to control unit economics.
[02:22] Maya Chen: exactly — commercially, the extension we're proposing is a 12‑month renewal with an uplifted reserved capacity bucket for EU onprem pilot + 30% headroom for burst. i'll show the numbers in the deck i send.
[02:33] Lena Voron: do you have a SLA for onprem? I mean uptime/latency guarantees?
[02:38] Samir Patel: for onprem we offer an operational runbook and we have a joint-support model — Redwood stands behind the runtime and we have response SLAs for sev1/sev2. for latency SLAs on onprem it's trickier — we can commit to certain targets if you run the supported instance types and follow the benchmark config — that's why the bench test is important.
[02:55] Tomás Ruiz: ok that makes sense. can you remind us the baseline instance shapes you recommend? we run AMD GPUs in EU-west.
[03:02] Samir Patel: we recommend A100 or equivalent for production for the larger LLMs. we have guidance for Ampere vs Radeon-type hardware; for AMD there are a couple of caveats on optimized kernels — you'll see notes in the ops doc. for EU-west specifically we usually test on A100 in the lab to model latency.

[03:20] (short crosstalk)
[03:24] Lena Voron: cost — is there a pricing delta for onprem vs hosted? basically are we paying infra + license + support?
[03:31] Maya Chen: yep — typical model is platform license + support + you own infra. For the pilot we can include a reduced license fee for the first 3 months to offset your setup cost, then revert to standard committed pricing tied to reserved capacity. I'll include a draft amendment with line items.
[03:46] Eva Martins: Procurement will need the exact amendment and line by line items, plus our legal's standard data processing addendum.
[03:52] Maya Chen: understood. we'll attach our DPA and the EU onprem addendum in the follow-up.

[04:05] Priya Singh: on the bench test — we want to push 1.2x our expected Q3 peak for 2 hours, with the full prompt set and KV cache warm. Can Redwood provide a test harness?
[04:15] Samir Patel: yes, we can run the harness — we usually run bench runs with continuous batching on the runtime, and measure p50/p95/p99 token latencies and throughput. I'll prepare a runbook for the harness that includes the container images, the traffic generator, and a perf dashboard.
[04:31] Priya Singh: great — also need to validate cold-start behavior for autoscaling, because our traffic is spiky at end-of-month.
[04:38] Samir Patel: autoscaling is configurable in the onprem manager — we expose thresholds and we recommend a small buffer of warmed K/V cache if you need low tail latencies. we'll include recommended autoscale profiles in the doc.

[05:00] Lena Voron: one more security ask — can logs be forwarded only to our SIEM via syslog? no third-party aggregation?
[05:06] Derrick Lee: yes, syslog or ES, you control the output endpoints. by default we don't ship to third parties unless you opt in.
[05:15] Tomás Ruiz: cool. about timeline — we want pilot in EU onprem started mid-May. does that align with Redwood timelines?
[05:22] Maya Chen: timeline looks plausible. if we close amendment by March 10, and we have a week for procurement PO, Samir's team can start staging in late March/early April for the pilot infra, then full onramp mid-May. there's some dependency on your infra provisioning and on HSM certs.

[05:40] (silence / note-taking)
[05:46] Eva Martins: procurement — we'll need a clear quote for budget in next two weeks. also legal asked whether there's any exclusivity or data sharing clauses in the new amendment?
[05:55] Maya Chen: no exclusivity by default. data sharing — we will not use your data to train models; we'll add the clause in the amendment.
[06:04] Priya Singh: practical thing — our team uses a mix of short prompts and long context threads; quantized model variants gave us different latency profiles. will Redwood swap in a smaller model variant as a fallback if nodes are saturated?
[06:16] Samir Patel: yes, we have routing policies and automatic fallback to compatible model variants — you can configure fallback thresholds by route. that's in the runtime config. sometimes token quality changes, so we'll work with you on evals before enabling.

[06:30] Tomás Ruiz: ok, what about monitoring and tracing — do you have distributed traces across the inference pipeline?
[06:35] Derrick Lee: we integrate with OpenTelemetry and provide per-request traces down to kernel-level latency if you enable the extra sampling. traces can be exported to your tracing backend.

[06:46] (customer asks about competitor pricing)
[06:50] Lena Voron: we had an offer from CloudScale that included managed appliances and a lower license for first year — any reason to prefer Redwood?
[06:59] Maya Chen: two quick points — first, our focus is on predictable unit economics for production (batching, KV caching and kernel selection) and second, our tooling for rollouts and fallbacks reduces risk when you change models. appliances are fine but they often lock you in — our k8s-based approach gives you more flexibility.
[07:20] Tomás Ruiz: fair.

[07:24] Samir Patel: backing up a bit — i will note a few technical gotchas: 1) AMD kernel parity for certain ops lags slightly, 2) keywrap edge case in old runtime i mentioned, and 3) autoscaler cooldown defaults may not be aggressive for high spikiness. we'll add tickets and proposed mitigations.

[07:44] Priya Singh: can you quantify the token cost savings we should expect once we move to reserved onprem? last time numbers were fuzzy.
[07:51] Maya Chen: rough rule of thumb: reserved reduces per-token platform fees by 25-40% depending on commit level; additionally, onprem removes the hosted egress component. we'll provide a spreadsheet with scenarios in the follow-up.

[08:05] (longer technical back-and-forth; timestamps jump)
[08:50] Samir Patel: ok i'll summarize the technical workstream: 1) Samir to share ops/install doc + terraform examples, 2) engineering bench test — Samir & Priya to coordinate, 3) perf tuning and autoscale profile draft, 4) security validation: HSM + DPA checks.
[09:10] Maya Chen: commercial workstream: 1) draft amendment for 12 months with capacity uplift and onprem addendum, 2) pricing spreadsheet and SOW line items, 3) procurement packet (PO path + legal redlines).
[09:25] Eva Martins: legal wants standard liability caps clarified for onprem installs — are they the same as hosted?
[09:31] Maya Chen: generally comparable but we'll flag the difference in the amendment and involve legal directly.

[09:42] (customer asks about rollback/fallback if pilot fails)
[09:46] Samir Patel: rollback plan is straightforward — you can switch routing back to hosted model in minutes, and we can keep a warm fallback pool in the hosted region for a short period. there are cost implications but it's supported.

[10:05] (discussion about support model & hours)
[10:12] Derrick Lee: for onprem customers we offer 24/7 critical support at enterprise tier, and standard daytime for pilot. we'll align with your SRE on escalation contacts.

[10:30] (brief silence)
[10:35] Priya Singh: one final prod detail: how are model patches handled for onprem? do you push updates or do we pull?
[10:41] Samir Patel: it's a customer-controlled upgrade — we provide signed images and a migration guide; push updates are only done with explicit approval.

[10:52] Maya Chen: ok great — want to do a quick recap and confirm owners.
[10:55] Lena Voron: yep, please.

[11:00] Maya Chen: recap — commercial: Maya will send amendment and pricing (owner: Maya, due 3/10). technical: Samir will send ops doc and bench run plan (due 3/7), Samir+Priya to schedule bench test (target w/c 3/17). procurement: Eva to confirm PO path (due 3/14). We'll also attach DPA and the EU onprem addendum.
[11:20] Eva Martins: thanks — i'll get internal approvals and loop legal.
[11:26] Tomás Ruiz: noted, will provision infra for testing once we have exact instance shapes.

[11:33] Maya Chen: perfect — we'll follow up with calendar invites for the bench test and a shared confluence space. any last questions?
[11:40] (brief)
[11:43] Lena Voron: none here, thanks.
[11:45] Maya Chen: thanks everyone — talk soon.

End of meeting (approx 52 minutes).

Notes on transcription: some words may be mistranscribed (eg 'KV cash' instead of KV cache), acronyms occasionally auto-corrected (SOC too), and speaker labels may shift in the auto transcript.
